source.version: Journal version: Vision Academica, Vol. 4, No. 3, 2026, pp. 1166-1183, DOI 10.70577/0p0tya49; received 2026-07-13, accepted 2026-08-05, published 2026-09-10 (PDF p. 1). The text says earlier versions of the manuscript reported a smaller effect size (PDF p. 12).
source.title_on_document: Impacto de la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa sobre la Originalidad Creativa y el Pensamiento Proyectual en Estudiantes de Diseño Gráfico

supplement.where: The document refers to no supplementary material or online appendix.

paper_design_summary: Quasi-experiment with 96 graphic design students in existing course sections (paralelos): 48 in an experimental group that received training in and used generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, DALL-E, Adobe Firefly) for research, ideation, alternatives, and concept development during an 8-week course, and 48 in a control group doing the same activities without AI. Two blind external judges scored pretest and posttest work with analytic 1-5 rubrics for creative originality (novelty, flexibility, elaboration, usefulness) and design thinking; groups were compared by ANOVA on the posttest. Assignment was not random.

studies.label: Quasi-experiment in graphic design course sections (8 weeks, pretest-posttest with control group)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Existing course sections (paralelos) assigned to an experimental condition (training in and use of generative AI tools in weeks 2 to 6) or a control condition (same activities with conventional design strategies, no AI).
assignment.quote: la asignación a los grupos control y experimental no fue aleatoria, sino determinada por los paralelos ya existentes de la asignatura, lo que corresponde a un diseño cuasi experimental
assignment.locator: PDF p. 15 (journal p. 1180), Limitaciones; also PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1172), Materiales y métodos: sample kept 'la organización natural de los grupos académicos'

arms.name: Experimental
arms.description: Training in generative AI (week 2) and use of ChatGPT, Midjourney, DALL-E and Adobe Firefly for research, ideation, generation of alternatives and concept development (weeks 3 to 6), same course content as control.

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Same content, activities, objectives and grading criteria, carried out with conventional design strategies and no AI assistance; no AI training.

participants.exclusions: Convenience sample. Inclusion required enrollment in the course, informed consent, and at least 80 percent attendance at intervention sessions; exclusion criteria were repeated absence, dropping out, or incomplete evaluation instruments. The paper reports only the final 96 (48 + 48) and does not say how many students were dropped under these criteria. ANOVA df (1, 94) match 96 analyzed.
participants.who: University students enrolled in a Graphic Design degree program (Diseño Gráfico); 54.2 percent female; 62.5 percent aged 18-21, 37.5 percent aged 22-25. Single institution and program.
participants.country: Not stated explicitly; authors are at Universidad Internacional SEK (Quito) and Universidad Nacional de Chimborazo (Riobamba), Ecuador.
participants.quote: La muestra quedó conformada por 96 estudiantes, distribuidos equitativamente en un grupo control (n = 48) y un grupo experimental (n = 48).
participants.locator: PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1172), Materiales y métodos; PDF pp. 10-11 (journal pp. 1175-1176), Table 4

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT, Midjourney, DALL-E, Adobe Firefly (model versions not stated)
ai_tool.how_used: Experimental group used the tools as support for research, ideation, generation of alternatives and concept development of course projects during weeks 3 to 6, after a training session in week 2. The paper says AI use was recorded by self-report. Tools include text chat and image generation, so the role could also be coded image_generation.

task.description: Graphic design course projects: problem research, AI-assisted ideation (experimental group), concept development, graphic proposals, critical evaluation. Pretest (week 1) and posttest (week 8) work scored with the same analytic rubrics. The paper does not describe the specific pretest/posttest task.

outcomes.name: Originalidad creativa (creative originality), posttest rubric score
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Analytic rubric, 1-5 scale, with four dimensions: novelty (originality of the proposal), flexibility (diversity of solutions proposed), elaboration (development and refinement), usefulness (relevance and functionality); the paper uses 'originalidad creativa' as a label for this composite creative performance. Scored double-blind by two external evaluators ('dos evaluadores externos', 'jueces externos'); their expertise is not stated, so expert_raters may apply. ICC = .98, exact agreement 96.9 percent. Dimension-level results are not reported. An ANCOVA with pretest as covariate is described only in words (group effect 'practicamente identico').
outcomes.delay: Posttest in week 8; AI use was in weeks 3 to 6 (Table 1 note). The paper does not say whether the scored posttest work was produced with AI available.

contrasts.reported: Posttest M ± DE: Control 2.65 ± 0.45, Experimental 4.12 ± 0.58 (pretest: Control 2.52 ± 0.40, Experimental 2.56 ± 0.44); n = 48 per group. ANOVA: F = 170.51, gl 1, 94, p < .001, η² = 0.65.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 11 (journal p. 1176), Table 5; PDF p. 12 (journal p. 1177), Table 6; group ns PDF p. 11, Table 4 and text

outcomes.name: Pensamiento proyectual (design thinking), posttest rubric score
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Analytic rubric, 1-5 scale, with four dimensions: research (problem understanding and information search), conceptualization (definition of design concept), ideation (generation and exploration of alternatives), evaluation (justification of design decisions). Same two blind external evaluators; ICC = .94, exact agreement 90.6 percent. Construct is design-process quality, not creativity as such.
outcomes.delay: Posttest in week 8; AI use was in weeks 3 to 6 (Table 1 note). The paper does not say whether the scored posttest work was produced with AI available.

contrasts.reported: Posttest M ± DE: Control 2.58 ± 0.40, Experimental 4.05 ± 0.61 (pretest: Control 2.45 ± 0.35, Experimental 2.51 ± 0.41); n = 48 per group. ANOVA: F = 186.57, gl 1, 94, p < .001, η² = 0.67.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 11 (journal p. 1176), Table 5; PDF p. 12 (journal p. 1177), Table 6

eligibility.reason: Assignment to AI was not random: groups were existing course sections (PDF p. 15, Limitaciones; PDF p. 7). 96 students analyzed (48 + 48), and the outcomes are rubric scores of student work by two blind external judges, so criteria 2 and 3 are met. Non-randomized comparison of people working with and without AI, so it is quasi_people, which the dataset folds into observational context. The experimental group also received AI training that control did not (confound noted by the authors).

one_line_finding: In a non-randomized comparison of two course groups (48 vs 48 graphic design students), the AI group scored higher on the posttest creative-originality rubric (4.12 vs 2.65 on a 1-5 scale; F(1, 94) = 170.51, p < .001, η² = 0.65; Tables 5 and 6, PDF pp. 11-12).
open_questions: Whether the scored posttest work was produced with AI available. Table 1 note limits AI use to weeks 3 to 6 and the posttest is in week 8 'utilizando los mismos instrumentos' as the pretest (PDF p. 8), which points to after_ai; the Discussion says the rubric focused on 'las propuestas finales' after 'ocho semanas de apoyo generativo continuo' (PDF p. 14), which points to with_ai. Coded with_ai and 'mixed' pending a decision.
Whether the two external judges count as expert_raters; their background is not stated.
The study institution is not named; country inferred only from author affiliations (Ecuador).
notes: Mixed-methods paper; the qualitative part has 4 focus groups (n = 24, 12 per condition), and a theme mentions risk of 'homogeneizacion estetica', but no diversity outcome is measured. Likert data on AI use and 'expanded creativity' were lost irrecoverably, so the planned PLS-SEM was not run (PDF pp. 6, 15-16). The authors say the effect size is much larger than in earlier versions of the manuscript, 'posiblemente por un error de trascripcion' in that earlier report (PDF p. 12). Spearman rho between the two posttest outcomes = .73, p < .001 (PDF pp. 12-13). Pretest equivalence: originality t = 0.18, p = .857; design thinking t = -0.65, p = .515 (PDF p. 11). Page locators give PDF page; journal page = PDF page + 1165.
